articles.title: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley of ‘60 Minutes’
articles.body: Mr. Pelley, a former “CBS Evening News” anchor, was ousted after months of tensions between staff and Bari Weiss, the network’s editor in chief.
articles.summary: CBS News fired Scott Pelley, longtime anchor of "60 Minutes" and former "CBS Evening News" anchor, amid months of reported tensions between staff and Bari Weiss, the network's editor in chief. The dismissal marks a significant personnel change at one of America's most prominent news organizations.

articles.title: Iowa hands Trump first major statewide primary loss of 2026 in governor's race
articles.body: Zach Lahn defeated Rep. Randy Feenstra in the Iowa Republican gubernatorial primary, marking President Trump's first major primary loss of the 2026 midterm election cycle.
articles.summary: Zach Lahn defeated Rep. Randy Feenstra in the Iowa Republican gubernatorial primary, marking President Trump's first major primary loss of the 2026 midterm cycle.

articles.title: Order Shielding Trump Family From I.R.S. Audits Will Remain, Blanche Says
articles.body: The acting attorney general said the administration was preserving a broad order protecting the president and his family from audits of already filed returns, despite dropping a $1.8 billion payout fund.
articles.summary: The Trump administration is maintaining an executive order that shields President Trump and his family from IRS audits of previously filed tax returns, according to acting attorney general Todd Blanche. The administration is nonetheless terminating a $1.8 billion payout fund, signaling a selective approach to reversing Biden-era policies.

articles.title: Out of Time to Delay, House to Vote on Trump’s Power to Continue War in Iran
articles.body: A measure to direct the president to halt U.S. engagement in Iran had been on track to pass in late May, but Republican leaders postponed action. They have run out of time to delay the vote.
articles.summary: The U.S. House is preparing to vote on legislation that would require the president to halt U.S. military engagement in Iran. The measure had been delayed by Republican leadership in late May but must now proceed to a vote as time runs out.

articles.title: Justice Dept. Won’t Proceed With Trump’s $1.8 Billion Fund, Blanche Says
articles.body: The acting attorney general told lawmakers that he would leave in place an order forcing the I.R.S. to drop investigations into President Trump, his family and his businesses.
articles.summary: The Justice Department will not pursue a Trump-related $1.8 billion fund, and the acting attorney general has confirmed he will maintain an order directing the IRS to cease investigations into Trump, his family, and his businesses. This signals a significant shift in federal enforcement posture toward the former president.

articles.title: Supreme Court Clears the Way for Republican-Friendly Map in Alabama
articles.body: In the first major case since the justices narrowed the Voting Rights Act, the court cleared the way for Alabama to use a map preferred by Republicans that leaves the state with only one majority-Black district.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has approved Alabama's use of a congressional redistricting map that reduces the state to a single majority-Black district, marking the first major case since the justices weakened the Voting Rights Act. This decision enables a Republican-preferred map and reflects the court's narrowed approach to federal voting protections.

articles.title: Deb Haaland Wins Nomination in New Mexico Governor’s Race
articles.body: Ms. Haaland, a former Interior secretary, took a big step toward making history as the first Native American woman to be a governor when she won the primary in her Democratic state.
articles.summary: Deb Haaland, the former Interior Secretary, won the Democratic primary in New Mexico's governor's race, putting her on track to potentially become the first Native American woman to serve as governor.

articles.title: Trump Aims New Tariffs at 59 Countries and the European Union
articles.body: Trump administration officials said they planned to impose levies of up to 12.5 percent on countries that failed to crack down on goods made with forced labor.
articles.summary: The Trump administration plans to impose tariffs of up to 12.5% on 59 countries and the European Union if they fail to enforce regulations against goods made with forced labor. The policy targets trade partners across multiple regions through a compliance-based tariff mechanism.

articles.title: Hamawy wins Democratic primary in race to replace Watson Coleman in New Jersey
articles.body: Adam Hamawy, a doctor and veteran, is the projected winner of the Democratic primary in New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, according to Decision Desk HQ. Hamawy locked down the nomination for the seat, which covers a large area of central New Jersey from Trenton to Plainfield, with 28.1 percent of the vote, per DDHQ. His...
articles.summary: Adam Hamawy, a doctor and veteran, won the Democratic primary in New Jersey's 12th Congressional District with 28.1% of the vote, securing the party's nomination for the seat covering central New Jersey from Trenton to Plainfield.

articles.title: Watch live: Rubio faces House questions over Iran, State Department budget
articles.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is back on Capitol Hill Wednesday morning, where he will face questions from the House Foreign Relations Committee about President Trump‘s fiscal 2027 budget request for the State Department and ongoing conflict with Iran. Rubio, in back-to-back hearings before a House and Senate panel on Tuesday, faced Democrats' ire over...
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio testifies before the House Foreign Relations Committee about the Trump administration's fiscal 2027 State Department budget and Iran policy, following contentious hearings with Democrats the previous day.

articles.title: Watch live: Bessent testifies before Senate on Treasury budget as affordability concerns rise
articles.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will testify Wednesday morning before the Senate Finance Committee on President Trump's fiscal 2027 budget request for the department. The White House is seeking $11.5 billion in budget authority for the Treasury Department’s domestic programs in 2027, a 12 percent decrease from 2026. The hearing comes as affordability concerns and the...
articles.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent testifies before the Senate Finance Committee on President Trump's fiscal 2027 budget request for the Treasury Department, which seeks $11.5 billion in domestic programs funding—a 12% decrease from 2026—amid rising affordability concerns.

articles.title: Graham Platner Meets With Senate Democrats Amid Texting Scandal
articles.body: Mr. Platner, the likely Democratic nominee for Senate in Maine, met in Washington with several senators. Chuck Schumer, the minority leader, dodged questions about his confidence in Mr. Platner.
articles.summary: Graham Platner, the likely Democratic nominee for Senate in Maine, met with several senators in Washington including Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. Schumer declined to directly address his confidence in Platner amid an ongoing texting scandal.

articles.title: Chan, Wiener face off for Pelosi House seat in San Francisco
articles.body: California state Sen. Scott Wiener (D) and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan, who enjoys former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s (D-Calif.) endorsement, are projected to go head-to-head for the retiring lawmaker's seat representing San Francisco in November, according to Decision Desk HQ. Wiener and Chan, running as a Democrat, defeated nine other candidates for spots in the November election....
articles.summary: California state Sen. Scott Wiener and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan have advanced to a November runoff for Nancy Pelosi's retiring House seat representing San Francisco. Chan has secured Pelosi's endorsement ahead of the general election.

articles.title: Even if Oil Prices Peak Soon, the Global Economy Will Slow This Year
articles.body: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, in a report, said the Middle East war’s consequences “are likely to be felt for some time.”
articles.summary: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned that the Middle East war will have prolonged economic consequences, and indicated that global economic growth will slow this year even if oil prices peak soon.

articles.title: War Games and Warnings on Strait of Hormuz Went Unheeded by Trump
articles.body: Over the past two decades, Iran repeatedly threatened to close down the waterway. President Trump underestimated Iran’s ability to do so.
articles.summary: Iran has repeatedly threatened over two decades to close the Strait of Hormuz, but President Trump underestimated the country's capability to execute such a blockade. The article indicates that prior warnings and war game scenarios about this threat went unheeded by the Trump administration.

articles.title: England do not need massive change after Ashes - Stokes
articles.body: Captain Ben Stokes insists England do not have to make a "massive change", despite their 4-1 Ashes hammering in Australia.
articles.summary: England captain Ben Stokes downplayed the need for major strategic overhaul after the team suffered a 4-1 loss in the Ashes cricket series against Australia, suggesting incremental adjustments rather than wholesale changes.

articles.title: N.B.A. Finals Introduce Music by Nicholas Britell and Nas
articles.body: The league is rolling out music by the composer Nicholas Britell and the rapper Nas that, if successful, could become the sport’s sonic shorthand.
articles.summary: The NBA is introducing new original music composed by Nicholas Britell and featuring rapper Nas for the NBA Finals. The league aims to establish this music as the sport's iconic sonic identity if the rollout proves successful.

articles.title: Sabalenka crumbles in quarter-finals in yet another French Open shock
articles.body: World number one Aryna Sabalenka sees her French Open title hopes vanish as she unravels in a crushing quarter-final defeat by Diana Shnaider.
articles.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka was knocked out of the French Open quarter-finals by Diana Shnaider in a shocking upset. Sabalenka's loss marks another unexpected exit for a top player at the tournament, dealing a blow to her title defense hopes.

articles.title: Late Night Wants Trump to Give Peace Talks a Chance
articles.body: “Oh, I’m sorry, is wrapping up the war you started not interesting enough?” Michael Kosta said on Tuesday, after the president called negotiations with Iran “boring.”
articles.summary: Michael Kosta, a late-night talk show host, criticized President Trump for dismissing peace negotiations with Iran as "boring," sarcastically implying the president should take diplomatic efforts more seriously rather than characterizing them as uninteresting.

articles.title: Party of 1: How Trump's ego destroyed America 250
articles.body: America’s 250th birthday could have been — should have been — a celebration to end all celebrations. The nation’s biggest birthday yet could have been an opportunity for both commemoration and recommitment, a festival marking a quarter millennium of democracy and a challenge to envision a bolder, better, brighter America for the generations to come.   Instead, we...
articles.summary: Opinion piece critiquing Trump's handling of America's 250th anniversary celebrations, arguing his ego undermined what should have been a unifying national commemoration of democracy and shared civic purpose.
